items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: I mean, you know, like Bessie Smith and Manly Smith and all of them.

ctx.x: Now what about in playing trumpet behind the singers? How did that develop?

Well, we used to do it. When the singer, singer, say and listen and cut out, we fill in. But now they go right along with the singer, you know what I mean? Like somebody say, I've got the blues and the blues about to kill me. I've got the blues and the blues about to kill me. And if I lose the blues, I won't be. You know what I mean? That's what we used to play. When the singer cut out, we come in. When she come back, we cut out. Drop under, you know. But now they go right along with the singer. Who would sing…
Did anybody use a plunger down here? Well, there was until after that.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: he played with the blues singers like Mamie Smith, Bessie Smith

ctx.x: He might have been sneaking out a lot of back doors too. Oh yeah. And nobody knew about it. So you couldn't figure it out then. Yeah you,

they had a, one I sometimes tried to prize me one time. Yeah you tell me about that. Yeah but I get the whiskey away and the boy told me look I didn't drink it. Everything down the bottle up. Mmhmm. What about that trumpet player that got paralyzed? Oh, oh he kicked a woman. And she told me before he kicked her with he'd never be no more good. Mmhmm. And he sure got a paralyzed all the way up. What was his name? Oh, I know his name too. He used to play with the thing for uh, Taylor. Taylor, that's his last name,…
That happened. I guess that shows you you shouldn't, you shouldn't kick women huh? That's right. You shouldn't have kicked that one I know.
